page: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server designed for high-density compute and parallel processing workloads. It features 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs based on the Hopper architecture, delivering a combined 637 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor with 104 physical cores and 208 vCPUs operating at 2.7 GHz. This setup is supported by 1872 GB of system memory, providing 9.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 6432 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 167331.13 and a PassMark CPU score of 125152.39. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 13661.0 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 431.78 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database and web serving capabilities are also highly rated, with Redis SET operations achieving 177.5 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 126.74 GB/sec. For large language model text generation, the system delivers 29.51 tokens per second on a medium 7B model and 3.7 tokens per second on a large 70B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the a3-edgegpu-8g represents a high-capital hardware class optimized for resource density rather than budget-friendly general-purpose compute. The inclusion of 8 dedicated enterprise GPUs and massive local NVMe storage results in a high resource-to-cost ratio, making it highly efficient for massive parallel processing but less suitable for workloads that cannot fully utilize the GPU accelerators. The system also lacks complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which may require additional networking configuration.
This server is engineered for demanding workloads such as large-scale machine learning training, LLM inference, high-performance computing, advanced ray tracing, and massive database operations.
